key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial carbon scavenger substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a sustainable route to improve photocatalytic carbon conversion by combining catalyst design for adsorption/charge separation with a bio-derived, carbon-negative co-reactant.
method: Use Cs/Ba to increase CO2 chemisorption and Bi to promote polarization and charge separation
Test photocatalysis with microalgae as sacrificial agent and compare against no sacrificial agent and microplastics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment may depend on maintaining stable microalgae availability and managing the coupled biology-photocatalysis process under real-world operating conditions.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
